summary: Lisa N. Owen specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. She completed her M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Texas at Austin by 2006, studying under doctoral supervisor Janice Leoshko, and also studied under Walter M. Spink in 1995.
Lita Peipina specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed an MA at the University of Oslo (attested 2008) under supervisor Jens Braarvig, and also studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

Litian Fang (1933–2014) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Peking University under Feng Youlan, Yongtong Tang, and Zhang Dainian (~1956–1961), and served as professor, doctoral supervisor, and founding director at Renmin University of China (~1961–2014).

Lloyd W. Pflueger works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He earned a doctorate from the University of California, Santa Barbara, and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University (attested 2015).

Lobsang Dargyay (1935–1994) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (~1952–1959), and the University of Munich, where he earned a Dr.phil. (~1970–1974).

Lobsang Gyatso (1928–1997) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied at Drepung Monastery (~1940–1959) and under Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso. He founded the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics in 1973, serving as its head (~1973–1997).

Lobsang Jamspal (born 1936) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Columbia University under Alex Wayman. His career includes posts at Delhi, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Columbia University (attested 1985–1990), and CIHTS.

Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa (1926–2008) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and later taught John W. Pettit.

Lobsang Shastri works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as Head Librarian at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 2003–2006) and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (attested 2018).

Lobsang Tendzin (born 1939) is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Drepung and Gyuto monasteries. He served as Chief Editor and Director at CIHTS (~1988–2000) and held leadership roles at LTWA.

Lobsang Tenpa specializes in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He earned a Master of Philosophy at Jawaharlal Nehru University under the supervision of Sharad K. Soni.

Lobsang Tenzin (born 1937) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Drepung Monastery. He served as abbot of Gyume Tantric College (attested 1987), director of CIHTS (1988–2001), and Chancellor of Sanchi University of Buddhist-Indic Studies.

Lobsang Yongdan is a Tibetology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Kumbum Monastery and earned a PhD from the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger (-2014). He held postdoctoral posts at the University of Bonn and MPIWG.

Loden Sherab Dagyab (born 1940) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Drepung Monastery and under teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, he was director of Tibet House New Delhi (1964–1966) and Tibetologist at the University of Bonn (1966).
Lodrö Chökyi Sengé studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche, and also taught Kalu Rinpoche.

Lodrö Sangpo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under supervisor Ernst Steinkellner. He founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996 and served as a senior teacher at Gampo Abbey (attested 2008).

Lokesh Chandra (1927–2022) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar educated at Punjab University and Utrecht University. He served as Director of the International Academy of Indian Culture and Chairman of the Indian Council of Historical Research (~2014–2017).
Longlian (1909–2006) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Fazun in 1939 and under traditional teacher Nenghai Shi from approximately 1941 to 1967.

Lore Sander (born 1936) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She studied under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1960–1967) and held positions at the Museum of Asian Art (1987) and Free University of Berlin (1994).

Lori Meeks (born 1976) specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Princeton (~1999–2003) under Jacqueline I. Stone and joined the University of Southern California as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies (~2004).
